title: Where to Start the Circuit
statement:
There are `n` fuel stations on a circular road, numbered `0` to `n - 1`. At station `i` you can take `gas[i]` units of fuel, and driving from station `i` to the next station `(i + 1) mod n` costs `cost[i]` units. Your tank has no size limit and starts empty.

Return the **smallest** station number you can start from (taking that station's fuel first) and drive once all the way round the circle, always in the same direction, without the tank ever going below `0`. Return `-1` if no start works.

examples.explanation: Starting at 0 or 1 you run dry. Starting at 2 the tank is 2 -2 = 0 after the first leg... and stays at or above 0 all the way round. (Station 3 also works, but 2 is smaller.)
There is only 3 units of fuel in total, but the whole circle costs 4.

hints.nudge: First ask whether ANY start can work. If the total fuel is less than the total cost, nothing can. If it is enough, where must a good start be?
hints.pattern: One pass: keep the running tank; whenever it goes negative, none of the stations since the last start can be a start, so restart from the next station.
hints.pseudocode:
total = 0; tank = 0; start = 0
for i in 0..n-1:
  gain = gas[i] - cost[i]
  total += gain; tank += gain
  if tank < 0: start = i + 1; tank = 0
return start if total >= 0 else -1
hints.walkthrough: Trying every start and driving the whole circle costs O(n^2). Think of gain[i] = gas[i] - cost[i]. If the total of all gains is negative there is not enough fuel anywhere: return -1. Otherwise some start works. Walk once through the stations while adding the gains. If the running tank first drops below zero at station i, then no station from the current start up to i could have been a good start (each of them would have had a tank at least as small, since they begin with less than the stretch before them leaves you with), so the next candidate is i + 1, with an empty tank. The last restart point is a valid start whenever the total is not negative; because a restart only happens when the tank becomes negative (strictly), it is the smallest station that works. O(n) time, O(1) memory.
